name: MonarchAiPromptInput
title: AiPromptInput
wrapsNative: TextField(_:text:prompt:axis: .vertical) with lineLimit(min...max), onKeyPress for Return and Escape, keyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command) on Send, PasteButton(supportedContentTypes:payloadAction:) and onDrop(of:isTargeted:perform:) for files, inside a bordered box with MonarchAiAttachmentTray, Button with .buttonStyle(.monarch(.primary, size: .sm)) for Send and MonarchAiStopButton
summary: The prompt box of an AI chat: a growing text field with attachments, a slot for the slash command or mention menu, a toolbar, a character and token count, and Send, which becomes Stop while a response runs.
whenToUse: At the bottom of an assistant conversation, in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom), where the person writes prompts and attaches files.
whenNotToUse: For person-to-person chat and ticket replies use MonarchMessageComposer, which has mentions, emoji, reply context and modes. For a single AI-assisted field in a form use MonarchAiAutofillField.

options.name: label
options.description: The accessible name of the field, such as "Message the assistant". Shown above the box with showsLabel.

options.name: text
options.description: The prompt. The app owns it, so it can keep and restore a draft.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the text is empty; the built-in "Send a message…" without it.

options.name: attachments
options.description: The attached files, shown by MonarchAiAttachmentTray inside the box. They allow sending without text.

options.name: acceptedContentTypes
options.description: The types the Paste button and drops hand to onReceiveFiles; other items are ignored.

options.name: submitOn
options.description: Which hardware-keyboard key sends: Return (Shift-Return adds a line) or only Command-Return. Command-Return sends with either.

options.name: minLines
options.description: The fewest visible lines.

options.name: maxLines
options.description: The lines the text grows to before it scrolls.

options.name: maxLength
options.description: The most characters. Shows the counter; over the limit sending is off and the box border turns to danger. The text is never cut.

options.name: warnAt
options.description: The share of maxLength at which the counter turns to the warning colour and the characters left are announced.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: A response is running: Send is replaced by MonarchAiStopButton and Escape on a hardware keyboard calls onStop.

options.name: showsLabel
options.description: Shows the label above the box.

options.name: disabledReason
options.description: Why the input is disabled, shown under it while .disabled(true) is applied.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the attachment tray's.

options.name: countTokens
options.description: Estimates tokens for the "≈ N tokens" readout. Called on every change, so keep it cheap.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Stops the running response, from Stop and Escape. Without it Stop is disabled.

options.name: onAttach
options.description: Adds the attach button. Present the app's PhotosPicker or fileImporter.

options.name: onReceiveFiles
options.description: Adds the system Paste button and accepts files dropped on the box, filtered by acceptedContentTypes. Load each provider and add it to attachments.

options.name: onRemoveAttachment
options.description: Removes an attachment by id. Without it the tray is disabled.

options.name: onRetryAttachment
options.description: Retries a failed upload by id.

options.name: triggerMenu
options.description: A menu above the box that reads and writes the same text, such as MonarchAiSlashCommands, or MonarchAiMentionContext with MonarchMentionQuery.find.

options.name: toolbar
options.description: Controls in the bar under the text, after the attach and paste buttons, such as MonarchAiPromptToolbar or MonarchAiModelPicker.

options.name: footer
options.description: Under the box, such as MonarchAiDisclaimer.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the text as typed. The field clears at once; if onSubmit throws, the text comes back unless something new was typed.

states.name: empty
states.description: The placeholder shows and Send is disabled.

states.name: typing
states.description: The text grows to maxLines and then scrolls; Send is enabled.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: The counter turns to the strong warning colour and the characters left are announced once.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: The counter and the box border turn to the danger colours, the counter is read as how many characters are over, and Send is disabled.

states.name: busy
states.description: Send is replaced by MonarchAiStopButton; Escape on a hardware keyboard stops.

states.name: dragging
states.description: While files are dragged over the box it takes the accent fill and border and shows "Drop files to attach".

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the subtle fill and border, disabled text and buttons, and the reason under the box.

appearance: A box in the surface background with the input border and the container radius, the focus ring while the field has focus, the subtle placeholder colour, and the primary Monarch button for Send. Dragging uses the accent subtle fill and accent border (the accent roles directly, because MonarchTone has no accent case); over the limit the border uses the danger border role. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web component keeps its own attachments and opens its own file input; on iOS, as on Android, the attachments are hoisted (attachments, onRemoveAttachment) because the app picks and uploads files with PhotosPicker or fileImporter. The web's paste of images into the text area becomes the system PasteButton, which reads the pasteboard without the paste permission prompt, and the web's drop becomes onDrop on the box; both hand NSItemProviders to onReceiveFiles (Android uses content URIs). SwiftUI's TextField cannot receive pasted images itself. The web's triggers and renderTriggerMenu become one triggerMenu slot; MonarchAiSlashCommands and MonarchAiMentionContext bind to the same text, so the slot needs no arguments (Android passes a TextFieldValue). Keyboard avoidance needs no option: SwiftUI keeps a view in the bottom safe-area inset above the keyboard (Android's keyboardPadding). Enabled is SwiftUI's .disabled(_:) instead of a parameter. The web's screen reader hints for Enter and Escape are not added: on a phone the on-screen Return adds a line and Send sends. The send and attach icons are fixed SF Symbols with their spoken names, instead of Android's icon slots. usePromptDraft has no counterpart: the app keeps the text binding.
accessibility: The text field is named by label; the visible label is hidden from VoiceOver so it is not read twice.
Send, Stop, Attach and Paste are standard buttons with spoken names ("Send", "Stop", "Attach files", the system's "Paste") and touch targets of at least 44 points.
The counter is read as "120 of 4000 characters", or as "3 characters over the limit" when over.
Reaching the warning share announces the characters left once; going over the limit is announced; returning is silent.
Dragging files shows "Drop files to attach" as text, not only the accent colours.
Dropping files has equivalents VoiceOver can reach: the Paste button and the Attach button.
Disabled: the reason is shown as text under the box.
edgeCases: White space alone does not enable Send; attachments without text do.
Text over maxLength is kept, not cut; only sending is blocked.
maxLines smaller than minLines is raised to minLines; minLines under 1 is 1.
If onSubmit throws after the person typed something new, the new text is kept and the failed text is not restored.
Dropped or pasted items of other types are ignored, and nothing is received while disabled.
At the largest text sizes the text grows taller and the counter and buttons stay in the bar.

examples.template:
MonarchAiPromptInput(
    {{label}},
    text: $prompt,
    acceptedContentTypes: [.image, .pdf, .plainText],
    maxLength: {{maxLength}},
    countTokens: { ($0.count + 3) / 4 },
    onAttach: {},
    triggerMenu: { EmptyView() },
    toolbar: { EmptyView() },
    footer: {
        Text({{footer}})
            .monarchTextStyle(.caption)
    },
    onSubmit: { _ in }
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiPromptInput(
    "Message the assistant",
    text: $prompt,
    acceptedContentTypes: [.image, .pdf, .plainText],
    maxLength: 4000,
    countTokens: { ($0.count + 3) / 4 },
    onAttach: {},
    triggerMenu: { EmptyView() },
    toolbar: { EmptyView() },
    footer: {
        Text("Answers can be wrong. Check important facts.")
            .monarchTextStyle(.caption)
    },
    onSubmit: { _ in }
)
